> [!reminder] How this scene works
> Nib explains the danger and the two jobs, and the Fell decide where to start. That decision is the only one in this scene, and it sets the order of the night.
> - **The river door.** Get two hundred Shrewish onto ten rafts and down the river. That is scenes 3 and 4.
> - **The shaft.** Go down under the warren with stone and wall off the root. That is scenes 5 and 6.
> - **Both.** The Fell split, and you run the two groups a scene at a time.
> Explain the floor clock to the table here, when the floor bulges, and draw it. The longer nobody is at the shaft, the more stone it will take to seal it. Nib is hiding where the shaft came from. The table can catch her lying, but she tells them only in scene 7.

> [!readaloud] Opening: The great hall
> Up the stairs is a long hall with a stone floor and a stone roof held up on stone pillars. It is packed wall to wall with Shrewish. Families sit on their bundles. Grandmothers sit on barrels. Children the size of rats run along the tops of the packs. Lamps hang from every pillar, and every face turns to look at you, and then up, and then further up. At the far end, a wide arch opens onto black water and a stone quay with rafts tied along it. You can hear the river.

> [!readaloud] Nib
> A Shrewish woman in a leather apron stands on an upturned bucket so she can see you better. Her paws are grey with old mortar to the elbow. She has a pencil behind each ear and a coil of rope over one shoulder, and she is looking at you the way a builder looks at a pile of bricks, working out where each of you goes.

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> "Right. I'm Nib. I built this place, every stone of it, so when I tell you it's coming down you can believe me. There's a root under us. A grey one, rotten, and it's growing up through the lower tunnels toward all these people, because that's what the grey does, it goes for anything warm. I can't stop it with what I've got, which is two hundred people who are knee-high to you and a lot of opinions."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> "So here it is. There are ten rafts at the river door and the river's the one road the roots can't shut. Somebody has to get everyone onto those rafts and off down the Sallowrun, and that's harder than it sounds, because half of them won't leave their larders. And somebody has to go down under the lower tunnels where it's coming up, with stone, and wall it off. It's a tight crawl. It was dug for me, not for you. But you can carry four times what I can, and I need stone more than I need anything."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *If asked what the Sallowrun is:* "The river. Big, brown, slow most of the year, fast tonight. It goes down to Quillbark Hold, which is a bark fortress full of quills and food, and they'll take us in, they always do, they just complain about it."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *If asked why Brackenmouth is stone:* "Because I'm Tooth-and-Tool, and so's everybody who dug here. We dig in clay and we build in stone, and we don't ask a root's permission to open a door. Everybody else on Shervinaw lives inside the roots and trusts them. Look where trusting them got the Slumpwood."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *If asked how the root got in when the walls are stone:* "There's an old drain under the lower tunnels. It must've cracked. That's all. Doesn't matter how, it matters that it's coming."

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *If asked what's in it for them:* "You'll have the thanks of two hundred Shrewish, and you'll have whatever you can carry out of my stores, and you'll have somewhere to sleep at Quillbark. That's not nothing. And if that's not enough, then you've got the fact that it's coming up under you as well."

> [!lorecheck] Lore: Quillbark Hold and the Tooth-and-Tool
> Any Fell who asks about a name Nib uses.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* Quillbark Hold is the great bark fortress of the river country, its walls grown full of quills, its larders deep enough to feed it for years. The Tooth-and-Tool are the Shrewish who would rather dig in clay and stone than live at a root's mercy, and the other Shrewish think they are half mad. Brackenmouth is the only stone warren on the whole world. *Then:* Their Lore increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* Quillbark Hold is a fortress downriver. The Tooth-and-Tool build in stone. Brackenmouth is the only warren like it.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* The names mean nothing to you. Nib explains them anyway, faster than you'd like.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You remember that Quillbark Hold turns away strangers at the gate. *Then:* It doesn't. Nib looks at them strangely if they say so.

> [!beat] The floor bulges
> Halfway down the hall the stone floor lifts. It rises slowly, the height of a hand, then a little more, in a long low hump running from the stairs toward the river arch. Two flagstones crack with a sound everyone hears. The whole hall goes silent. A baby somewhere starts crying, and then the floor settles back down, almost flat.

> [!lorecheck] Logic: Which way it's growing
> Any Fell who watches the bulge.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* The hump runs straight from the stairs to the river arch. Whatever is under there is growing toward the river door, toward the rafts, and it's moving faster than Nib thinks it is. You can also tell where it starts: right under the lower tunnels, at one point. It's coming up out of a hole. *Then:* Their Logic increases by 1. Tell the table that the floor clock is real and that waiting will cost them stone.
> - **Success.** *Read:* It runs from the stairs to the river arch. It's growing toward the rafts.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* The floor moved. That's all you can tell.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You're sure it's moving away from the river, toward the back of the warren. You say so, and a few Shrewish believe you and start carrying their bundles the wrong way. *Then:* They come back by themselves when the floor moves again.

> [!lorecheck] Vigilance: Watching Nib
> Any Fell who watches Nib while she talks about the drain.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* She calls it an old drain, but she knows exactly how deep it goes, how wide it is and which way it bends, and nobody knows that about an old drain. Her paws are shaking, and her eyes keep going to the stairs down to the lower tunnels and away again. She's lying, and it is costing her. *Then:* Their Vigilance increases by 1. This Fell knows Nib is hiding something about the shaft. Read [[07 - Nib's Secret|Nib's Secret]] knowing the table may raise it before then.
> - **Success.** *Read:* She knows more about that drain than she's saying.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* She's tired and frightened like everyone else here.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You decide Nib is planning to run and leave everyone. *Then:* She isn't. She stays to the end on every route.

> [!secret] What Nib is hiding
> There is no old drain. Last spring Nib dug a shaft under the lower tunnels looking for clean water, broke into a hollow, and struck a mother root nobody had mapped. It was already grey. She plugged the shaft with clay because stone would have taken until summer, and told no one. The root broke through the clay tonight. If the Fell press her now, she says only, "Later. Ask me later, and I'll tell you, I promise. Right now I need stone." She tells them in [[07 - Nib's Secret|Nib's Secret]].

**This applies to a Shrewish Fell.** Nib talks to them first, as one Shrewish to another. When she lies about the drain to a Shrewish, she cannot look at them, and any Fell watching sees it with no roll.

> [!dialogue] Old Furze
> *From the back of the hall, loud and creaky:* "I'm not leaving forty years of pickles for a crack in the floor, Nib Sorrelgate, and nor is anybody else down the bottom end, so you can stop shouting."

> [!dialogue] Dobb
> *From the river arch, counting:* "Raft one, raft two, raft three, all tied, all dry, twenty a raft and no standing up. Ten rafts. Two hundred. Ten rafts."

> [!reminder] Every route
> The Fell can go two ways, and they may split. Write down where each Fell starts.
> - **The river door.** Get the Shrewish out of their larders and onto the rafts. Go to [[03 - The Larders|The Larders]], then [[04 - The River Door|The River Door]]. The rafts start going out. The floor clock fills one segment at the end of each scene while no Fell is at the shaft.
> - **The shaft.** Go down under the lower tunnels with stone. Go to [[05 - Down the Shaft|Down the Shaft]], then [[06 - The Grey Mother|The Grey Mother]]. The sooner they get there, the less stone it takes to seal it: 2 loads plus the floor clock.
> - **Split.** Some Fell go each way. Run the two roads in turns, a scene of each. The floor clock moves only when no Fell is at the shaft.
> Nib goes with whoever goes to the shaft. If nobody does, she goes alone with a bucket of mortar, and the Fell find her halfway down when they get there.

> [!choice] Where the Fell start
> - **The river door.** Go to [[03 - The Larders|The Larders]].
> - **The shaft.** Go to [[05 - Down the Shaft|Down the Shaft]].
> - **Both.** Each Fell picks a road. Say where each one is.
> - **Neither.** Nobody here has time for that. Nib hands each Fell a sack of mortar and points. If they still won't go, the hall floor lifts again under their feet, and a crack runs from the stairs toward the river arch. Give them the choice again.

> [!readaloud] Closing: Two jobs
> Nib hops down off her bucket and starts handing out rope. Somewhere at the back of the hall, Furze is still arguing. At the river arch Dobb is still counting. Under all of it, the hum in the floor has not stopped once.

> [!beat] Where everyone is now
> Say where each Fell is: on the stairs down to the lower tunnels with Nib, or headed for the larders and the river door with Kettle running ahead. Kettle goes with whoever goes to the river.
